content.intro: Operators combine values into expressions. Parentheses, precedence, strict comparisons, and deliberate fallback behavior help prevent expressions that compile but communicate the wrong intent. In this lesson, focus on bitwise and, or, xor, and not; then compare it with bit shifts. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use bitwise operators and other specialized operators when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.

common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
